日.name: Sun
日.meaning: The <radical>sun</radical> radical is the same shape, so this one is easy: the kanji means <kanji>sun</kanji>, and because the sun makes each day, it also means <kanji>day</kanji>.
日.reading: The sun shines into にち, a niche in your wall, every single day. When it's used as "day" on its own, the reading is often ひ instead, like a sunny heel print. Learn にち first.

一.name: One
一.meaning: A single flat line. One line, one thing: <kanji>one</kanji>.
一.reading: Picture one long line of ants marching across the floor, and you have いち, an itch. One ant is fine. One line of them makes you itch all over.

人.name: Person
人.meaning: Two legs walking along: a <kanji>person</kanji>. Same as the <radical>person</radical> radical.
人.reading: A person is being chased by a genie: じん. The genie wants to grant three wishes, but the person just wants to be left alone. You'll also meet にん, as in 三人 (three people).

年.name: Year
年.meaning: A <radical>slide</radical> lands on something <radical>dry</radical>. It takes a whole <kanji>year</kanji> of sunshine for a waterslide to get that dry.
年.reading: A nun (ねん) goes down the dry slide once a year, on her birthday. Every year the other nuns cheer.

大.name: Big
大.meaning: It's the <radical>big</radical> radical: a person with arms stretched out wide, showing how <kanji>big</kanji> something is.
大.reading: How big is it? As big as a die the size of a house, だい. Roll it and the whole town shakes. (Before some words it's たい, and as a word, おおきい.)

十.name: Ten
十.meaning: A <radical>cross</radical>, which is also the number <kanji>ten</kanji> in Japanese. Two lines crossing, like the X of Roman numeral ten tipped on its side.
十.reading: Ten juice boxes, じゅう, stacked in the shape of a cross. Someone thirsty drank ten of them in a row.

二.name: Two
二.meaning: Two lines, <kanji>two</kanji> things. The top one is shorter, so they don't look like a single fat line.
二.reading: You have two knees, に. Point at each knee: "one knee, two knee."

本.name: Book
本.meaning: It's the <radical>book</radical> radical: a tree (<kanji>木</kanji>) with a line near its roots. Books are made from the bottom of trees, and the kanji means <kanji>book</kanji>. The mark at the root also gives it the meaning "origin".
本.reading: A goose flies up and honks (ほん) at you every time you open a book. Books make it angry.

中.name: Middle
中.meaning: A <radical>stick</radical> skewers a <radical>mouth</radical> right through the <kanji>middle</kanji>.
中.reading: It was a chew toy, ちゅう, stuck in the middle of the stick. The dog chews and chews but can't get it off.

山.name: Mountain
山.meaning: The <radical>mountain</radical> radical: three peaks. As a kanji it means <kanji>mountain</kanji>.
山.reading: The sun (さん) rises over the mountain. On its own the word for mountain is やま, but in names of mountains you'll hear さん, as in 富士山.

出.name: Exit
出.meaning: A <radical>mountain</radical> pokes up out of a <radical>container</radical>. It can't stay in there, so it takes the <kanji>exit</kanji>.
出.reading: It comes out with a bang, like the start of a shoot-out: しゅつ. As a verb, でる means to go out.

三.name: Three
三.reading: Three suns, <reading>さん</reading>, lined up in the sky. It's very hot.

見.name: See
見.meaning: An <radical>eye</radical> on a pair of <radical>legs</radical> walks around town just to <kanji>see</kanji> things.
見.reading: What does the walking eye see? Me! み, as in 見る (to see). In compounds it reads けん, like Ken getting spotted.

月.name: Moon
月.meaning: Same as the <radical>moon</radical> radical. The moon goes round once a <kanji>month</kanji>, so it means both.
月.reading: A gecko, げつ, climbs up to the moon every month. For month names it's がつ: 一月 is January.

生.name: Life
生.meaning: The <radical>life</radical> radical as a kanji: <kanji>life</kanji>, a sprout pushing out of the dirt.
生.reading: Life sets sail, せい, on the day it's born. Also read しょう, as in 一生 (a whole life).

五.name: Five
五.reading: Five goats, ご, standing on each other's shoulders.

上.name: Above
上.reading: A joker, じょう, pops up above ground and wiggles the toe. As a word, うえ means "above".

四.name: Four
四.meaning: An <radical>enclosure</radical> with <radical>legs</radical> inside. A table seen from above has <kanji>four</kanji> legs.
四.reading: It's a pen with a sheep, し, in it. し also sounds like death, so people often say よん instead.

金.name: Gold
金.meaning: The <radical>gold</radical> radical: <kanji>gold</kanji>, which also means money.
金.reading: A king, きん, sits on a pile of gold.

九.name: Nine
九.meaning: A <radical>swan</radical> goes down a <radical>slide</radical>. Swans have nine lives (not cats, whatever you heard): <kanji>nine</kanji>.
九.reading: Line up the swans like balls and hit them with a cue stick, きゅう. Nine in the pocket.

入.name: Enter
入.meaning: The <radical>enter</radical> radical: a person ducking to <kanji>enter</kanji> a low doorway.
入.reading: The first to enter is a newt, にゅう. As a verb, はいる is to enter.

子.name: Child
子.meaning: The <radical>child</radical> radical: <kanji>child</kanji>, a baby with arms out.
子.reading: The child is chasing a sheep, し. On its own, a child is こ.

学.name: Study
学.meaning: A <radical>child</radical> under a <radical>lid</radical> with <radical>sparkle</radical> coming off the top. The kid is <kanji>study</kanji>ing so hard their head is sparking.
学.reading: A goose honks "がく!" every time the child gets an answer right.

円.name: Yen
円.meaning: A frame with a line through it. It's a Japanese coin, the <kanji>yen</kanji>, and coins are round, so it also means <kanji>circle</kanji>.
円.reading: It's read <reading>えん</reading>, which is where the English word "yen" came from.

八.name: Eight
八.meaning: Two strokes spreading apart, like the bottom of the number 8: <kanji>eight</kanji>.
八.reading: Eight hatchets, はち, thrown at a target.

六.name: Six
六.meaning: A <radical>top hat</radical> sits on top of <radical>eight</radical>. Take off the hat to pull out two rabbits, and eight becomes <kanji>six</kanji>.
六.reading: Six rocks, ろく, fall out of the hat instead.

下.name: Below
下.reading: What's down there? A car, か, buried underground. Also げ, and as a word, した (below).

気.name: Spirit
気.meaning: <radical>Steam</radical> rises and <radical>slide</radical>s off into the air. It's the <kanji>spirit</kanji> leaving the kettle.
気.reading: The spirit locks itself in with a key, き. You'll see it in 元気 (healthy) and 天気 (weather).

小.name: Small
小.reading: A showman on stage, しょう, pulls out a tiny, tiny rabbit. The crowd has to squint.

七.name: Seven
七.meaning: A <radical>swan</radical> crosses the <radical>ground</radical>. Swans lay <kanji>seven</kanji> eggs, and this one is carrying them across.
七.reading: It carries them on a sheet, しち. You'll also hear なな, and people often use it to avoid mixing up しち with いち.

女.name: Woman
女.reading: Your cousin Joe, じょ, is a woman. It's short for Josephine. The word on its own is おんな.

白.name: White
白.reading: A hacker, はく, types on a pure white screen. The everyday word is しろ.

百.name: Hundred
百.meaning: One (<radical>ground</radical>) on top of <radical>white</radical>. White hair means you're <kanji>hundred</kanji> years old, give or take one.
百.reading: A hundred-year-old hacker, ひゃく, still coding. Watch for びゃく and ぴゃく when it's counted: 三百, 六百.

先.name: Ahead
先.meaning: Someone with a tuft on their head running on long legs. They always get <kanji>ahead</kanji> of everyone else.
先.reading: They're first to the prize: a single cent, せん. In 先生 (teacher), the teacher is ahead of the class.

名.name: Name
名.meaning: In the <radical>evening</radical> it's dark, so you open your <radical>mouth</radical> and shout your <kanji>name</kanji> so people know who you are.
名.reading: A maid, めい, hears you and writes your name down on a card. You'll also see みょう in 名字 (surname).

川.name: River
川.meaning: The <radical>river</radical> radical: <kanji>river</kanji>, three lines flowing downhill.
川.reading: A cent coin, せん, floats down the river. As a word, river is かわ.

千.name: Thousand
千.meaning: Something <radical>slide</radical>s off a <radical>cross</radical>. A cross is ten, and the slide adds zeroes: <kanji>thousand</kanji>.
千.reading: It's a thousand cents, せん, sliding off in a pile.

水.name: Water
水.reading: Water turns into something sweet, すい, when you add enough sugar. The word on its own is みず.

男.name: Man
男.meaning: <radical>Power</radical> in the <radical>rice paddy</radical>: a <kanji>man</kanji> working the field. (That's the old picture. You can do better.)
男.reading: He's a dancer, だん, actually, and he dances in the mud. The everyday word is おとこ.

木.name: Tree
木.meaning: The <radical>tree</radical> radical: <kanji>tree</kanji>, and the <kanji>wood</kanji> it's made of.
木.reading: A mocking bird, もく, sits in the tree mocking you. On its own a tree is き, as in "a key hanging from a tree".

校.name: School
校.meaning: Kids <radical>mix</radical> together under a <radical>tree</radical>. The tree is where the old village <kanji>school</kanji> met.
校.reading: The teacher is a koala, こう, who teaches from up in the tree. 学校 is school.

土.name: Soil
土.reading: A door, ど, in the ground opens up and soil pours out. 土曜日 is Saturday.

車.name: Car
車.reading: A shark, しゃ, is driving the car. It's the only way it gets around on land. The word on its own is くるま.

天.name: Heaven
天.meaning: Something <radical>big</radical> with one extra line above it. The only thing above big is <kanji>heaven</kanji>.
天.reading: Up in heaven, the angels play tennis, てん. 天気 is weather.

火.name: Fire
火.reading: Your car, か, is on fire. 火曜日 is Tuesday. The word on its own is ひ.

右.name: Right
右.meaning: An <radical>awning</radical> over a <radical>mouth</radical>. You eat with your <kanji>right</kanji> hand under the awning of the food stall.
右.reading: An owl hoots "う" from your right shoulder. The word for right is みぎ.

左.name: Left
左.meaning: The hand reaching out on top, and <kanji>工</kanji> (craft) below: the hand that holds the work still while you craft. For most people, that's the <kanji>left</kanji>.
左.reading: In your left hand is a saw, さ. You're not very good at sawing. The word for left is ひだり.

休.name: Rest
休.meaning: A <radical>person</radical> leaning against a <radical>tree</radical>: taking a <kanji>rest</kanji>.
休.reading: They rest their cue stick, きゅう, on the tree too. 休む is to rest.

雨.name: Rain
雨.reading: An owl hoots "う" miserably in the rain. The everyday word is あめ.

国.name: Country
国.meaning: A <radical>jewel</radical> inside an <radical>enclosure</radical>. A <kanji>country</kanji> puts a fence around its treasure.
国.reading: It keeps the jewel sealed with a cork, こく. The word on its own is くに.

長.name: Long
長.meaning: The <radical>long</radical> radical: <kanji>long</kanji>, like long flowing hair. The one with the longest hair is the <kanji>leader</kanji>.
長.reading: The leader hands out chocolate, ちょう, a really long bar of it. 社長 is company president.

時.name: Time
時.meaning: The <radical>sun</radical> next to a <radical>temple</radical>. Temples ring bells as the sun moves, to tell the <kanji>time</kanji>.
時.reading: At that time a jeep, じ, drives past the temple. 一時 is one o'clock. The word とき means "time" too.

行.name: Go
行.reading: Where will you go? To pet a koala, こう. As a verb, いく. You'll also meet ぎょう, as in 行 for a line of text.

後.name: Behind
後.meaning: <radical>Going</radical>, but slowly: a <radical>cocoon</radical> dragging along in <radical>winter</radical>. It's always <kanji>behind</kanji> the others.
後.reading: A goat, ご, is right behind it, pushing. 午後 is afternoon. Also あと (after) and うしろ (behind).

前.name: Front
前.meaning: <radical>Eight</radical> <radical>moon</radical>s and a <radical>knife</radical>. Eight moons ago you stood at the <kanji>front</kanji> of the line with a knife. Nobody argued.
前.reading: You were a zen monk, ぜん, very calm about it. 午前 is morning. The word まえ is "in front".

間.name: Interval
間.meaning: The <radical>sun</radical> peeks through the gap in a <radical>gate</radical>. That gap is the <kanji>interval</kanji>, the space between.
間.reading: A kangaroo, かん, squeezes through the gap. 時間 is time. The word あいだ is "between".

東.name: East
東.meaning: The <radical>sun</radical> rising behind a <radical>tree</radical>. That's the <kanji>east</kanji>.
東.reading: A toad, とう, sits in the tree to watch the sunrise. 東京 is Tokyo, the eastern capital.

今.name: Now
今.meaning: A <radical>person</radical> with a roof over their head and one line under them, standing right here, <kanji>now</kanji>.
今.reading: "いま!" You shout "Eee! Ma!" and want your mom now. 今 on its own is "now". In compounds it's こん, as in 今日 ... which is actually read きょう. Japanese.

高.name: Tall
高.meaning: A <radical>top hat</radical> on a <radical>mouth</radical> on a <radical>helmet</radical> on another mouth. It's a <kanji>tall</kanji> tower.
高.reading: A koala, こう, climbs up the tall tower. 高校 is high school. As a word, たかい means tall and expensive.

外.name: Outside
外.meaning: It's <radical>evening</radical> and your <radical>toe</radical> is poking out of the tent. It's cold <kanji>outside</kanji>.
外.reading: A guy in a fedora, がい, is waiting outside. 外国 is a foreign country. The word そと means outside.

来.name: Come
来.meaning: A tree with its branches held out, waving you over: <kanji>come</kanji> here!
来.reading: A lion, らい, comes out of the tree. 来年 is next year. As a verb, くる.

話.name: Talk
話.meaning: You <radical>say</radical> things with your <radical>tongue</radical>. That's how you <kanji>talk</kanji>.
話.reading: Wave a wand, わ, and people start talking. 電話 is a telephone. 話す is to talk.

北.name: North
北.meaning: Two people sitting back to back to stay warm. It's the <kanji>north</kanji>.
北.reading: They're playing hockey, ほく, on the frozen lake. The word on its own is きた.

午.name: Noon
午.meaning: It's like <kanji>牛</kanji> (cow) without the horn on top. At <kanji>noon</kanji> the cow puts its horn away and naps.
午.reading: A goat, ご, sneaks in and eats the cow's lunch. 午前 and 午後: morning and afternoon.

書.name: Write
書.meaning: A <radical>brush</radical> over the <radical>sun</radical>. You <kanji>write</kanji> all day while there's light.
書.reading: You write with a shovel, しょ, because the brush is too small. 書く is to write.

半.name: Half
半.meaning: A <radical>drop</radical>, <radical>two</radical> and a <radical>cross</radical>, all cut down the middle by one line. Everything is in <kanji>half</kanji>.
半.reading: Your hand, はん, does the cutting. 半分 is half.

西.name: West
西.meaning: A box with a lid and two legs inside. The cowboys keep their gold in it out <kanji>west</kanji>.
西.reading: They sail, せい, west to find more. Also さい, and にし on its own.

電.name: Electricity
電.meaning: <radical>Rain</radical> over a field with a tail sticking out. The rain brings lightning, and lightning is <kanji>electricity</kanji>.
電.reading: The lightning hits a dentist, でん. His drill runs forever now. 電話 is telephone, 電車 is train.

語.name: Language
語.meaning: You <radical>say</radical> things with your <radical>mouth</radical> in <radical>five</radical> different ways. That's five <kanji>language</kanji>s.
語.reading: A goat, ご, speaks all five. 日本語 is Japanese, 英語 English.

聞.name: Hear
聞.meaning: An <radical>ear</radical> pressed against a <radical>gate</radical>. You're trying to <kanji>hear</kanji> what's inside.
聞.reading: You hear someone eating a bun, ぶん. 新聞 is a newspaper. 聞く is to hear (and to ask).

食.name: Eat
食.meaning: The <radical>eat</radical> radical: <kanji>eat</kanji>. A lid on a bowl of food.
食.reading: Eating gives you a shock, しょく, because it's so hot. 食べる is to eat; 食事 is a meal.

何.name: What
何.reading: "なに?!" That's the word for what. Picture a nanny shouting it. Before some sounds it shortens to なん, as in 何時 (what time).

南.name: South
南.meaning: A <radical>cross</radical> on top of a <radical>helmet</radical> with something <radical>dry</radical> inside. It's a desert explorer's helmet, and they're heading <kanji>south</kanji>.
南.reading: They snack on naan bread, なん, the whole way. 南 on its own is みなみ.

万.name: Ten Thousand
万.meaning: A hook dangling from a line. It's hooking a <kanji>ten thousand</kanji> yen note.
万.reading: A man in a suit, まん, grabs it. Japanese counts in ten thousands: 一万, 十万.

毎.name: Every
毎.meaning: A <radical>gun</radical> pointed at a <radical>mother</radical>. She gets held up <kanji>every</kanji> day on the way to work, and she's had enough.
毎.reading: She fights back with a microphone, まい, feeding back so loud the robber runs off. 毎日 is every day.

母.name: Mother
母.reading: Mom's on a boat, ぼ. The word for your own mother is はは; someone else's is おかあさん.

読.name: Read
読.meaning: You <radical>say</radical> the words out loud to <radical>sell</radical> the story. You <kanji>read</kanji> it to an audience.
読.reading: Your audience is a doctor, どく, who falls asleep. 読む is to read.

友.name: Friend
友.meaning: A <radical>hand</radical> reaching out to a <radical>stool</radical>. You offer your seat to a <kanji>friend</kanji>.
友.reading: Your friend plays the ukulele, ゆう, while sitting on it. 友だち is a friend.

父.name: Father
父.meaning: Two strokes on top and a cross below, like a dad with his arms waving in the air: <kanji>father</kanji>.
父.reading: He's waving because he stepped on a hoof, ふ. The word for your own father is ちち.
